title: A combustion calorimetry measurement
stem: In a constructed trial, $0.62\,\mathrm{g}$ of an alcohol of molar mass $46\,\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ burns completely below a copper can. The $200\,\mathrm{g}$ of water in the can warms by $12.5\,\mathrm{K}$. Use $4.18\,\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ for water and initially neglect all other heat capacities.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the experimental molar enthalpy of combustion.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain how heat absorbed by the copper can affects this experimental result.

steps.text: $q_{\mathrm{water}}=mc\Delta T=$ $10450\,\mathrm{J}$.
The amount of fuel burnt is $0.0135\,\mathrm{mol}$.
$\Delta H_{\mathrm{c}}=-q_{\mathrm{water}}/n=$ $-775\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$.
Some released heat warms the can. Ignoring this energy underestimates the heat released, so the reported enthalpy is less negative than the value accounting for the can.

subject: chemistry
title: Extrapolating a cooling trace
stem:
A constructed experiment mixes reagents at time zero. Before mixing both were at 20 °C. After the reaction has finished, the following linear cooling data are recorded. Total solution mass is $100\,\mathrm{g}$; $0.05\,\mathrm{mol}$ reacts. Use $4.18\,\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$.

| Time after mixing / min | Temperature / °C |
|---|---|
| 2 | 27.16 |
| 3 | 27.04 |
| 4 | 26.92 |
| 5 | 26.8 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use the linear post-reaction trend to estimate the temperature at time zero and the corrected temperature rise.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the corrected molar enthalpy change.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: State the purpose and one limitation of this correction.

steps.text: The cooling gradient is $-0.12\,\mathrm{K\,min^{-1}}$; extrapolate the same line to zero time.
The intercept is 27.4 °C, giving $7.4\,\mathrm{K}$ for the corrected rise.
$\Delta H=-mc\Delta T/n=$ $-61.9\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$.
It estimates heat lost during the reaction by extending the cooling trend backwards.
It assumes that the cooling behaviour after the reaction represents heat loss during mixing and reaction; this may fail if heat-loss rate or the apparatus conditions change.

title: An endothermic dissolution
stem: A constructed soluble molecular solid has molar mass $60\,\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$. A $4\,\mathrm{g}$ sample dissolves completely to form $104\,\mathrm{g}$ of solution, whose temperature falls by $2.6\,\mathrm{K}$. Assume specific heat capacity $4.18\,\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ and no heat exchange with the surroundings.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the heat change of the solution and the molar enthalpy of dissolution.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain the sign of this enthalpy change.

steps.text: $q_{\mathrm{solution}}=mc\Delta T=$ $-1.13\times10^{3}\,\mathrm{J}$, since the temperature change is negative.
The amount dissolved is $0.0667\,\mathrm{mol}$.
$\Delta H_{\mathrm{sol}}=-q_{\mathrm{solution}}/n=$ $17\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$.
The dissolving system absorbs energy from the solution; its enthalpy increases, so dissolution is endothermic and the value is positive.

subject: chemistry
title: System and surroundings entropy
stem: A constructed thermodynamic model gives the system enthalpy change as $-40\,\mathrm{kJ}$ and system entropy change as $-100\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ for a specified extent of reaction at $300\,\mathrm{K}$. The surroundings form a large heat reservoir at that temperature. Pressure is constant, and the reservoir entropy change is $-\Delta H_{\mathrm{system}}/T$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the entropy change of the surroundings and the total entropy change.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the feasible direction and relate the result to the system Gibbs energy change.

steps.text: The reservoir entropy change is $133\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$.
The total entropy change is $33.3\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$.
The forward direction is feasible: the total entropy change is positive.
$\Delta G_{\mathrm{system}}=-T\Delta S_{\mathrm{total}}=$ $-10\,\mathrm{kJ}$. Its sign gives the same conclusion.
